answer: Each identity bonds 60 credits to the cipher ledger at a chosen inlet. Its fixed nectar pool is 600 credits per epoch, split among cipher-valid identities; an auditor recomputes the split and burns any duplicate cipher receipt's bond. One honest identity locks 60 and can take all 600 nectar. A second fake locks 60 more yet adds zero to the attacker's total; the thousandth fake still locks 60, lifts the locked total to 60,000, and cuts each fake's share to 0.6 nectar. A pool-flooding ring fails: it locks 60 per fake for a fixed 600 nectar total, while honest identities use uncrowded inlets.
